run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The incident is about production-us-east-2, but this Run's Kubernetes access covers only the production-eu-west-2 cluster, and both Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, traces_search, traces_list_services). The only data that actually belongs to production-us-east-2 is therefore the app-260-prod-logs index, which holds exactly 10 documents in the authorized window (8 tagged cluster=production-us-east-2, 2 tagged production-eu-west-2). In that index the checkout-service 500s in production-us-east-2 are preceded and accompanied by payment-service 504s whose own error text names the upstream payment provider stripe-us: "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms" (07:45:20Z and 09:00:20Z, correlation_id chk-us-2142), followed by checkout 500s "payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)", "payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway", and "circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)", plus a payment-service WARN "Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031". A checkout latency WARN (p95 1700ms vs 800ms target) predates the 500s at 06:45:20Z. The same index shows the same two services in production-eu-west-2 reporting health (checkout p95 230ms, "Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms"), and the production-eu-west-2 cluster objects I could read are consistent with that: checkout and payment deployments 1/1 ready and the checkout pod logging only successful payments 09:17Z-09:45Z. So the deepest cause the evidence supports is degradation of the external stripe-us payment provider, with payment-service timeouts and circuit breaking as the mechanism and checkout-service HTTP 500s as the observed customer-facing symptom; Kubernetes-side causes in production-us-east-2 (restarts, config/flag settings there) could not be checked and remain unknown.

claims.text: app-260-prod-logs contains exactly 10 documents with timestamps inside 2026-11-21T09:45:30Z-2026-11-22T09:45:30Z, spanning 2026-11-22T06:45:20Z to 09:40:20Z: cluster=production-us-east-2 8 docs, cluster=production-eu-west-2 2 docs; service=checkout-service 6 docs, service=payment-service 4 docs; level ERROR 6, WARN 2, INFO 2; status_code 500 x4, 504 x2, 200 x4. This is log-document coverage, not a request or error rate.

production-us-east-2 checkout-service logged WARN at 2026-11-22T06:45:20Z (correlation_id chk-us-2001): "Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)" with status_code 200 - latency was already above target before the first 500.

At 2026-11-22T07:45:20Z under the same correlation_id chk-us-2142 in production-us-east-2: checkout-service ERROR status_code 500 "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)" and payment-service ERROR status_code 504 "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms".

production-us-east-2 payment-service logged a second ERROR status_code 504 "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms" at 2026-11-22T09:00:20Z and WARN at 09:30:20Z "Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031".

production-us-east-2 checkout-service logged status_code 500 at 2026-11-22T08:45:20Z "circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)" (chk-us-2208), at 09:15:20Z "payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway" (chk-us-2252), and at 09:40:20Z "circuit-breaker open for payment-service" (chk-us-2280).

Affected: checkout-service in production-us-east-2 - its own four ERROR records with status_code 500 on POST /api/checkout (07:45:20Z, 08:45:20Z, 09:15:20Z, 09:40:20Z) plus its p95 1700ms WARN at 06:45:20Z are its own failure evidence.

Affected: payment-service in production-us-east-2 - its own two ERROR 504 records (07:45:20Z, 09:00:20Z) naming stripe-us /v1/charges and its WARN at 09:30:20Z reporting Stripe-US degraded mode with retry queue depth=1031.

The same index carries two production-eu-west-2 records in which these services report health: checkout-service INFO 2026-11-22T07:45:20Z "Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes" and payment-service INFO 08:45:20Z "Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms" - the eu-west-2 region shows no failure in the data I read.

In the production-eu-west-2 cluster (the only cluster this Run's Kubernetes access covers), otel-demo deployments checkout and payment are each 1/1 ready, and pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged at 09:17:47Z-09:45:21Z repeated "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and order-confirmation lines with no error lines in the returned window.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config read in the production-eu-west-2 cluster defines fault flags paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable") plus productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad; every flag in that file has state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off", so no fault is switched on in the config that was read.

Rejected: the fault-injection flags visible in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (production-eu-west-2) explain the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s - every flag read there is defaultVariant "off", and eu-west-2's own records show checkout healthy at p95 230ms, Stripe-EU normal and successful payments in the checkout pod logs. The us-east-2 flagd config was not readable, so this rejection covers only the config I could read.

Hypothesis (unresolved): a configuration or fault-injection setting inside the production-us-east-2 cluster (its own payment/checkout or flagd configuration) could have produced the payment failures; the observed pattern (30s upstream timeouts plus an explicit "degraded mode acknowledged via status page" note) points more to the external provider than to a deterministic local failure flag, but no object in production-us-east-2 could be read to confirm or exclude it.

Hypothesis: the checkout-service 500s were amplified by payment-service retry backlog (depth 1031 at 09:30:20Z) and by checkout's own circuit breaker opening at failure rate 41% above its 25% threshold; whether checkout would have fully recovered without that pressure is not observable from the available evidence.

Advice: confirm current status of the stripe-us payment provider (the payment-service WARN itself refers to a provider status page) and, if the degradation persists, evaluate shifting production-us-east-2 payment traffic to the Stripe-EU path that these records show as normal, as a human decision rather than an automated change.

Advice: pull production-us-east-2 Kubernetes state (checkout/payment deployment and pod status, container last termination reasons, its flagd/config configuration) and Prometheus error-rate and latency series, none of which were reachable in this Run, before closing the incident.

gaps: production-us-east-2 Kubernetes state is not readable in this Run (Kubernetes access is production-eu-west-2 only), so the us-east-2 checkout/payment Deployments, pod status, restart/termination history, events, Services, endpoints, networkpolicies and ConfigMaps (including its flagd fault flags) are unknown - no claim about them is possible.

Prometheus was unreachable: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket values, error rates and latency histograms for checkout/payment in either cluster are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and two traces_search calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span evidence exists on which service called which, and no parent-child call edge from checkout to payment or payment to stripe-us can be asserted from traces.

app-260-prod-logs holds only 10 documents covering 2026-11-22T06:45:20Z-09:40:20Z; nothing is present before 06:45:20Z inside the authorized window, so the true onset of the degradation and any earlier background errors are unknown.
The four checkout 500 records are log documents, not a request count or error rate; the actual share of failed checkouts and the number of affected customers are not measurable from this evidence.

No frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator or other service logs exist in the index beyond the two services listed, so customer-facing impact beyond checkout-service's own 500 responses is unverified.

Whether stripe-us is degraded provider-side or unreachable from payment-service's network path cannot be separated: the evidence is payment-service's own timeout message and a WARN referring to a provider status page; no direct stripe-us telemetry is available.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deployment or configuration change record can be correlated with the 06:45-09:40Z degradation.
next_steps: Obtain Kubernetes read access to production-us-east-2 and inspect checkout/payment Deployment and Pod status, container lastState termination reasons, events and the us-east-2 flagd/config settings.
Restore or query Prometheus for production-us-east-2 error-rate and p95 latency series for checkout and payment to establish when the deviation began and its magnitude.
Query Jaeger for checkout->payment and payment->stripe-us spans in production-us-east-2 to confirm the call edge and timeout duration.
Confirm with the payment provider's status reporting whether stripe-us was degraded in the 06:45-09:40Z window, and decide manually whether to fail over to the Stripe-EU path.

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
